title: Writing for himself, practice and audience appeal
summary: Carter plans material and practice time, a possible suite or concerto, and wants audience appeal.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: practical considerations? How many musicians should I use, or are you thinking more in terms of ...
I'm thinking more in terms of at this moment of material.

And of my own playing, you know, because I want to be in a good ... well, what is it I want to say? I want to be as well up on the instrument as I can be, and when I sit down and write, you know, I've got to think also if I'm gonna write maybe 6 hours a day, I better put aside 2 hours a day to practice, if I'm not playing in a club or something. You know, I've got to play the instruments, too.

Well, what is that like? That is, we hear about somebody like Duke Ellington, for example, so able to write for certain musicians. What's it like to write for yourself if you're the featured musician?
Well, the thing is, Duke Ellington wasn't too much a featured musician.

He was, as he called himself, 'I'm just the piano player!' -- and Duke, as we know, was no slouch as a piano player, but he did write for the musicians and he always knew for whom he was writing -- he could be writing for Lawrence or for Johnny or for Coote for Carney or for Poole or for Kearney, you know. What's it like to be writing for myself? I would like

That's part of the decision, too --what I'm gonna play, you know. I would like to do something in the nature of a suite for a saxophone or, what you might call a concerto or something, you know -- something that wouldn't be too challenging technically, because I don't know how much practice time I'm gonna be able to put in, you know?
But I don't want to do anything to attempt to just display my ... what's the term I want to use?
Well, I was trying to shy away from that word, because I ...

All right. Artistry, you know, is good. But I'd like to do something that might also be an artistic success for me, and maybe, and very happily, a commercial success, you know, for the sponsor. I would like the audience to have -- I mean for the album to have reasonably fair audience appeal.

Uh huh. So that's a consideration, which a lot of people, I think, or a lot of, let's say, academic people types wouldn't consider maybe a compositional decision, but I don't see why not, I mean, that's -- indeed, that is a compositional decision.
